svg.title: Contract selection and who pays
svg.text: No procedure master list. The procedure
arrives as text on the Booking and is kept
As received from the surgeon's rooms
Short codes and snippets, exactly as sent.
Replaces the rooms' text when it arrives;
the Booking's change history keeps the original.
The wording the invoice prints, its own field:
the rooms', replaced by the hospital's, then
Admins can edit it as free text, and
Each Procedure on the Booking gets
for reference on a fixed price
No Contract yet? The Booking shows
the patient, or a parent or guardian
The payer is billed when the Contract bills
the payer. The insurer or funder only
suggests a path; it never narrows the list.
Every Procedure has exactly one Contract: it sets how the work is priced and who gets the invoice.
Each Contract is one priced item with its own settings. A holder's schedule becomes many Contracts.
A hospital, an insurer or funder, a
anaesthetist, or AA. Holds the billing
name and details and how invoices
Bills its holder, or the payer?
Default RVG code · Active or Disabled
Fixed price, in dated price ranges
No setting is dated: a change is an audited edit, and a change from a date means a new Contract. Only a fixed price has dates.
No contract · RVG is offered first on every List and never expires. Every destination has one open-price
fallback, made by the system and picked with Other price, such as Prepaid · Fixed price or Forte · SXAP · Fixed price.
A surgeon group's fixed fees bill the payer, so they sit under Patient, linked to the surgeons they cover (OQ-105).
New prices from 1 Oct, sent 5 Nov: Face lift gains a price range from 1 Oct at $3,200 ($3,100 from 1 Jun before).
Kept by the office from her list, offered only on her Lists. Picking it starts the prepayment letter and invoice.
A prepaid Contract is never priced from RVG units, and the anaesthetist never overrides its price (OQ-96).
Each item of the hospital's SXAP schedule is a Contract tagged SXAP, its code kept as the holder reference code.
Offered only on CES Lists. Forte's plain RVG Contract, Forte' SXAP, sits the same way under Forte › SXAP.
An insurer billed directly at plain RVG, offered on every List. Many insurance jobs look like this.
At booking setup the office says where the
invoice goes, then picks the Contract.
Example: a facelift on Lowe's List at St George's.
Active Contracts that fit the List: held by its
hospital, linked to its surgeon or anaesthetist,
or an insurer's or funder's with no links; and
only where their specialties include the
Worked out from each Contract's settings.
Patient means the payer on the Booking.
Prepaid starts the prepayment. Under the
hospital, its tags; under Special, the Contract.
Type to search names, codes, invoice
No contract · RVG is pinned first. Or flip
Other price to pick the fallback, and type
On an RVG price: the RVG code, time and
modifiers. On a fixed or open price: an RVG
code for reference only, no time or modifiers.
The Booking's insurer or funder marks one
The anaesthetist can change the Contract
Until the List is authorised, from the same
Contracts, no reason needed. Each change
is audited, flagged at office review and
clears a typed price. Pre-approval fell
through on the day? Change to
No contract · RVG and the payer is billed.
Procedure: text as received, no master list·Contract: one per Procedure, picked on the step rail·Who pays: the Contract's own settings decide
